slides.title: Slides that teach, not decorate
slides.subtitle: What the evidence says about deck design, and what a script can check
slides.notes: This deck is built by build-deck.js from sample-spec.json and checked by deck-check.js. Every number in it comes from the research brief of 2026-09-25.

slides.title: What the research supports
slides.notes: First, the design choices with real evidence behind them. Then, the ones that turn out to be lore.

slides.title: Putting labels next to what they describe had the largest effect
slides.alt: Bar chart of four effect sizes: labels placed next to the graphic 0.63, pleasant color and faces 0.39, signaling what matters 0.38, and slides versus no slides 0.07.
slides.source: Effect sizes (d or g): Schroeder and Cenkci 2018; Brom et al. 2018; Alpizar et al. 2020; Baker et al. 2018
slides.notes: Spatial contiguity, meaning a label placed on the thing it names, beat the other design effects here at g = 0.63 across 58 comparisons. Slides versus no slides at all is essentially zero: the tool does nothing, the design does.

slides.title: Cut what is irrelevant, not what is warm

left.head: The evidence says cut
points: The full script on the slide

slides.notes: Minimal is not the finding. Relevance is. Emotional design raised retention, and printed key terms beat both the full script and nothing.

slides.title: The strongest evidence is broad, and the famous rules are thin

stats.label: participants across 29 reviews of multimedia design
small audience studies behind sentence headlines

slides.source: Noetel et al. 2022; Garner and Alley 2013; 2023 Shanlax study; searches of 2026-09-25
slides.notes: The overview of reviews is huge. The assertion-evidence format rests on two small studies, one run by its own author. The 6x6 rule has no traceable study at all.

slides.title: What a script can check
slides.notes: Now the file itself. Some defects are invisible until PowerPoint lays the slide out.

slides.title: A slide render hid twenty lines of overflowing text
slides.alt: Slide render showing ten lines of body text reaching the bottom edge of the slide; the other twenty lines are cut off with no visible sign.
points: PowerPoint measured 1,197 pt of text in a 342 pt box
slides.notes: This is why the checker measures instead of looking. The overflow went past the slide edge, so the picture of the slide simply does not show it.

slides.title: Six checks run on every deck before it ships
points: Text fits its box and the slide
Body text is 18 pt or larger
Every slide has a unique title
Every picture and chart has alt text
slides.notes: All six are measured through PowerPoint itself, and each one has a canary and a live check that proves it fires.

slides.title: Build the story first, then let the checker argue
points: Write sentence titles and read them alone as the storyline
Build with build-deck.js, check with deck-check.js
Review the renders with fresh eyes
slides.notes: Titles first, then evidence, then the machine checks, then a human look.
